correctness.rationale: A specified m-side vertex has success exactly q times the parity-separated collision-free path sum. Conditional unused local decisions remain independent; collisions terminate a unique functional path, so no missing alternatives. The log falling-factorial expansion yields the Gaussian exponent (1/alpha+1/beta)t²/8, Gaussian tail gives Riemann-sum justification, and first-revisit decomposition yields the fixed-q constant. Exact rational enumeration in verify.py checks m,n=(1,1),(1,2),(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(2,4),(3,3),(3,4) for q=1/2 and 1/3; finite checks do not establish asymptotics.

value.rationale: The representational loss from cycles is a naturally decision-relevant efficiency quantity for transitive delegation, independent of whether the group gets the right outcome. This theorem provides exact finite expectation for every community-size imbalance, a sharp square-root density boundary for effective representation, a continuous crossover law depending on community proportions, and an unexpected O(1) total loss at fixed direct-voter density. The precise invariant is motivated by cycle-induced disenfranchisement rather than arbitrary counting.
